title: quantization-experiment-notes-temp
content:
Sprint-era scratchpad for quick experiments and oddball findings when trying low-bit quantization configs on small benchmark workloads. NOT a final spec; backup or toss after lab repros.

Objective:
- Quick notes for reproducing surprising perf/quality delta when enabling 4-bit quantization with per-channel vs per-tensor scaling on our nominal Llama-like v2 test model.

Short summary of runs (rough):
- run-2025-02-11-a: 8-bit baseline (dequant CPU fallback) — latency 42 ms median, top-1 quality baseline.
- run-2025-02-12-b: 4-bit per-tensor symmetric — latency 29 ms median, hallucination rate up ~6% on narrow prompt set.
- run-2025-02-18-c: 4-bit per-channel asymmetric + re-centering — latency 31 ms, hallucination rate reduced vs per-tensor but still +2% vs 8-bit.
- run-2025-02-25-d: mixed-precision: activations fp16 + weights 4-bit PC — latency 30 ms, cost win but occasional token-level artifacts on long-context prompts.

Notes / hypotheses:
- Per-channel scales appear to preserve distribution tails better; improves generation coherence on questions with numeric tokens. Might be helping KV cache interactions.
- Re-centering (zero-centering small outlier scales) helps on arithmetic prompts but increases variance on conversational prompts.
- We saw one reproducible failure mode when sequence_length > 1024 and attention window tuning was disabled: repeated tokens after token 750 for run-c. Hypothesis: kernel math accumulation overflow in low-precision path.
- Batching showed non-linear perf: 4-bit single-request latency improves but throughput per GPU decreases for tiny sequences due to kernel launch overhead. Good candidate for runtime batching heuristics.

Quick checklist for next lab runs:
- [ ] Add a run with per-channel 4-bit + stochastic rounding enabled in quantizer (config qcfg-stoch-01).
- [ ] Re-run failing long-context case with accumulation using 32-bit accumulator and trace internal logits at each step.
- [ ] Validate outputs against the eval harness (eval/qa-regression-2025) and capture diff for hallucination metric.
- [ ] Try mixed-precision with attention kernel fallback disabled to see if artifacts correlate.

Commands/notes used during experiments:
- local runner: python infra/bench/run_local.py --model model-v2-test --quant 4pc --batch 1 --seq 2048 --trace-steps 10
- quick check: jq '.metrics | {latency_ms, tokens_generated}' results/*.json | head

Temporary artifacts (where to look):
- raw logs: gs://redwood-temp/quant-exps/2025-02-*/
- harness: /workspace/evals/qa-regression-2025/
- small reproducible prompt set attached as prompts/long-context-repro.txt in this folder (temp)

Random ideas for follow-ups (brain-dump):
- schedule a 30m sync with SRE kernel owners to review overflow hypothesis; bring sample traces.
- measure memory fragmentation when toggling per-channel quant -> does allocator behavior matter for latency?
- consider lightweight calibration pass on a representative prefix set rather than global statistics.

If you use this doc to formalize anything, copy into confluence/eng-serving-runtime/quantization-notes and change status to in_review.

-- Liam
